research_update.subtitle: 2026-09-07 · speed-governor geometry · seed replication complete
research_update.headline: Watching an arc instead of a straight corridor lowers crashes at every density.
research_update.summary: The filter only ever scales the commanded speed; it never steers. Three evaluation seeds (523, 527, 531) x five bar densities were re-run with the corridor replaced by the arc the vehicle will actually fly. The arc tube had the lowest crash rate in 15 of 15 seed-density cells, pooling to -1.49 pp [-1.90, -1.08] against the risk cap with no seed heterogeneity (I2 0%). Widening that tube to 1.2 m helps twice over, while widening the straight corridor destroys the mission.

corridor_token.definition: A corridor token is a compact description of one locally traversable opening between obstacles. The current obstacle token says where a bar surface is; a corridor token says where the drone may fit, how wide the opening is, and how far that opening remains clear.
corridor_token.why_now: The geometry was real and the actor consumed it safely: K=6 expanded the observation from 898 to 946 dimensions without changing historical offsets. It reduced bar contact by 0.93pp, but capture improved only 1.57pp and its confidence interval crossed zero. That rules out simply extending this same run; the next representation must preserve more depth structure rather than add more copies of the same local gap summary.

success_criteria.headline: Success is held-out capture rate at a stated density -- never a PPO loss curve.

primary.definition: fraction of held-out episodes ending with the pursuer within 0.5 m of the target
primary.measured_by: eval_navrl_v2_density_sweep.sh -- a frozen checkpoint replayed on episodes it never trained on
primary.why: Training-time capture mixes densities while the curriculum ramps, so it cannot be compared across epochs. A held-out sweep fixes the density per cell.

secondary.definition: episodes ending in a bar/wall collision
secondary.role: the dominant failure mode; a capture gain paid for with more crashes is not progress

secondary.definition: episodes reaching the step limit without capture
secondary.role: separates 'could not find the target' from 'found it and crashed'

secondary.definition: episodes touching an obstacle at any point
secondary.role: sensitivity to representation changes even when capture is flat

not_success_metrics.why: Reward falls when the density curriculum promotes, so a declining curve during an active curriculum measures rising task difficulty, not a worsening policy. Only compare reward WITHIN one fixed density.
PPO's surrogate and value losses are optimizer diagnostics on a moving target distribution. They do not decrease monotonically in a healthy run and carry no task-performance meaning.
Entropy is not task success. For this squashed Gaussian, however, a sudden plunge far below its normal range is a latent-tanh saturation alarm and must be read with KL.
Guardrails only. KL flags too-large policy steps (rollback at 0.04); explained variance flags a critic that has stopped tracking returns. Both being healthy is necessary, never sufficient.

curriculum_gate.what: density promotion gate (a TRAINING control, not a result)
curriculum_gate.rule: promote +15 bars when capture over a 16,384-episode window clears the threshold, using the measured knot schedule 0.82@70, 0.77@85, 0.72@100, 0.70@115+, and only after at least 1,000 PPO epochs at the current density
curriculum_gate.why_ramped: A flat threshold strands the curriculum forever once the achievable capture ceiling falls below it -- the failure mode behind the v1 100-bar plateau. Demand mastery where the task is easy; relax where it is hard.
curriculum_gate.caution: The rolling 50-epoch tail shown in Live is a diagnostic, not this gate. Never quote the tail as a promotion or publication number.

success_criteria.checkpoint_rule: Evaluate a curriculum run with last_gen_ppo_ep_*.pth. gen_ppo.pth is the best-REWARD checkpoint, and reward peaks at low density, so it is a sparse-density policy that scores near 15% when replayed at high density.

perception_robustness.finding: Detection latency looked like the dominant failure axis (-42.7pp at 0.1s) until the cause was isolated: a delayed detection was a vehicle-frame measurement from t-tau being lifted to world with the pose at t, so the drone's own motion entered every filter correction -- 0.23m from translation and 0.41m from yaw, against the 0.15m of target motion. Buffering the pose beside the detection and lifting with it recovers 94% of the 0.1 s loss. Under exact timestamp/pose history the residual at 0.1 s is -2.5 pp; longer delays remain material (-15.8 pp at 0.5 s), so latency is not generally benign.
